subtopics.title: Reliable Transfer over a Perfectly Reliable Channel (rdt1.0)
subtopics.summary: The baseline case where the underlying channel never corrupts or loses packets; the sender and receiver FSMs need no feedback, sequence numbers, or retransmissions. Serves as the starting point for incrementally adding reliability mechanisms.

subtopics.title: Reliable Transfer over a Channel with Bit Errors (rdt2.x)
subtopics.summary: Introduces ARQ mechanisms: checksums for error detection, ACKs/NAKs, and retransmission on negative feedback. Covers handling corrupted ACKs/NAKs by adding sequence numbers (rdt2.1) and eliminating NAKs by ACKing the last correctly received packet (rdt2.2).

subtopics.title: Reliable Transfer over a Lossy Channel (rdt3.0)
subtopics.summary: Handles lost packets and premature timeouts using a countdown timer and retransmission, with sequence numbers letting the receiver detect and discard duplicates. Shows why alternating-bit sequence numbers suffice for stop-and-wait operation.

subtopics.title: Stop-and-Wait Performance and Channel Utilization
subtopics.summary: Quantifies how stop-and-wait wastes bandwidth (e.g., only 267 kbps effective throughput on a 1 Gbps link) and derives utilization as a function of RTT and L/R, motivating the shift to pipelined operation.

subtopics.title: Go-Back-N (GBN) Protocol
subtopics.summary: Pipelined sliding-window protocol allowing up to N unacknowledged packets, using cumulative ACKs and retransmitting all outstanding packets after a single timeout; the receiver discards out-of-order packets.

subtopics.title: Selective Repeat (SR) Protocol
subtopics.summary: Pipelined protocol in which the receiver individually acknowledges and buffers out-of-order packets while the sender retransmits only missing packets; covers per-packet timers and window-size constraints relative to the sequence-number space.
